locator: §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators, paragraph beginning “Do not write expression = NULL”
claim: NULL represents an unknown value, and because it is not known whether two unknown values are equal, NULL = NULL does not yield true.
quote: Do not write expression = NULL because NULL is not “equal to” NULL. (The null value represents an unknown value, and it is not known whether two unknown values are equal.)

locator: §2 Operators, and Parse-Affecting Attributes, paragraph “All operators generally evaluate to NULL”
claim: SQLite documents that operators generally evaluate to NULL when any operand is NULL, except for specific stated exceptions, in accordance with the SQL92 standard.
quote: All operators generally evaluate to NULL when any operand is NULL, with specific exceptions as stated below. This is in accordance with the SQL92 standard.

locator: SELECT, WHERE clause, first paragraph after “WHERE condition”
claim: PostgreSQL keeps a row only when its WHERE condition evaluates to true, and eliminates any row that does not satisfy the condition.
quote: where condition is any expression that evaluates to a result of type boolean. Any row that does not satisfy this condition will be eliminated from the output. A row satisfies the condition if it returns true when the actual row values are substituted for any variable references.

claim: SQLite includes only rows whose WHERE expression evaluates to true, and excludes rows for which it evaluates to either false or NULL.
quote: If a WHERE clause is specified, the WHERE expression is evaluated for each row in the input data as a boolean expression. Only rows for which the WHERE clause expression evaluates to true are included from the dataset before continuing. Rows are excluded from the result if the WHERE clause evaluates to either false or NULL.

claim: SQLite has no separate Boolean storage class; it stores Boolean values as integers 0 (false) and 1 (true).
quote: SQLite does not have a separate Boolean storage class. Instead, Boolean values are stored as integers 0 (false) and 1 (true).

claim: AND yields false whenever either operand is false, even if the other is unknown; it yields unknown when neither operand is false and at least one is unknown, so true AND unknown is unknown.
quote:
a       b       a AND b   a OR b
  ------- ------- --------- --------
  TRUE    TRUE    TRUE      TRUE
  TRUE    FALSE   FALSE     TRUE
  TRUE    NULL    NULL      TRUE
  FALSE   FALSE   FALSE     FALSE
  FALSE   NULL    FALSE     NULL
  NULL    NULL    NULL      NULL

locator: §2 Operators, and Parse-Affecting Attributes, paragraph “When paired with NULL”
claim: SQLite's AND evaluates to false when one operand is NULL and the other is false, and its OR evaluates to true when one operand is NULL and the other is true.
quote:
When paired with NULL:
  AND evaluates to 0 (false) when the other operand is false; and
  OR evaluates to 1 (true) when the other operand is true.

claim: OR yields true whenever either operand is true, even if the other is unknown; it yields unknown when neither operand is true and at least one is unknown, and false only when both operands are false.
quote:
a       b       a AND b   a OR b
  ------- ------- --------- --------
  TRUE    TRUE    TRUE      TRUE
  TRUE    FALSE   FALSE     TRUE
  TRUE    NULL    NULL      TRUE
  FALSE   FALSE   FALSE     FALSE
  FALSE   NULL    FALSE     NULL
  NULL    NULL    NULL      NULL

claim: NOT yields false for true, true for false, and unknown for unknown.
quote:
a       NOT a
  ------- -------
  TRUE    FALSE
  FALSE   TRUE
  NULL    NULL

locator: §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators, paragraph beginning “Ordinary comparison operators”
claim: An ordinary comparison with a null operand yields null, signifying unknown, rather than true or false, for both = and <>.
quote: Ordinary comparison operators yield null (signifying “unknown”), not true or false, when either input is null. For example, 7 = NULL yields null, as does 7 <> NULL. When this behavior is not suitable, use the IS [ NOT ] DISTINCT FROM predicates:

locator: §2 Operators, and Parse-Affecting Attributes, paragraph beginning “The IS and IS NOT operators”
claim: In SQLite, when one operand is NULL and the other is not, IS evaluates to false and IS NOT evaluates to true, and an IS or IS NOT expression cannot evaluate to NULL.
quote: If one operand is NULL and the other is not, then the IS operator evaluates to 0 (false) and the IS NOT operator is 1 (true). It is not possible for an IS or IS NOT expression to evaluate to NULL.
